title: Canonical internal-module trace coefficient interfaces
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring, $R_Z=\Lambda_Z$ its pulled-back ring on the small pro-etale site of a scheme $Z$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $D(Z)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_Z})$ the ordinary unbounded internal-module derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with relative derived tensor and unit $R_Z$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For a scheme map $h:Z\to B$, use the published aliases $\operatorname{tracePull}_h=Lh^*$ and $\operatorname{tracePush}_h=Rh_*$ for the total derived module functors [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Put $\operatorname{TraceLoc}(Z)=\operatorname{Loc}(\operatorname{Dbc}(Z,\Lambda))$, with exactly the constant-model bounded constructibility predicate [sk-def-sfb-constructible] and localizing closure [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside its fixed algebraic closure, at coefficients $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ put $\operatorname{traceTate}(Z)=R_Z(1)[2]$, the integral Tate module of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] placed in degree zero and shifted by $2$. The ordinary internal-module inverse image has the specified strong monoidal core characterized uniquely by the universal tensor-section normalization: the adjunction unit sends the universal tensor of two sections to the tensor of their universal pullback sections, and the unit comparison on the regular module is the coefficient map $\alpha_h$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction]. Denote this predicate by $\operatorname{CondensedTensorNormalization}$, its published unique-existence helper by $\operatorname{condensedTensorCore\_existsUnique}$, the core selected from that unique-existence theorem by $\operatorname{condensedTensorCore}$, and its induced monoidal structure by $\operatorname{condensedUpperStarMonoidal}$. The canonical unit comparison $\operatorname{condensedDerivedUnitIso}:Lh^*R_B\simeq R_Z$ is computed in degree zero from this normalized ordinary unit map, using the existing derived-to-complex comparison and the single-complex functor. All these are the existing declarations in Sheaf.Paper.TraceBaseChangeFirst; no assertion about either trace triangle is part of this interface.
